questions.question: If a student drops an item near a stopped bus, they should:

options.text: Hurry and pick up the item.
Leave the item behind.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Have another student pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: It is dangerous for students to pick up dropped items. The driver may not see them and could move the bus. Students should stay away from the bus's danger zones. They should get the driver's attention and ask the driver to pick up the item.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is considered an encroachment?

options.text: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
A driver executing a single pull-up.
A driver placing the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake.
The vehicle stalling while the driver shifts gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the test. Every encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Before operating a school bus, ____ should be checked.

options.text: The left mirror
The right mirror
All mirrors
The inside mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: All mirrors
questions.explanation: School bus drivers must check all mirrors before driving. You need to see the maximum viewing area around the bus. Adjust mirrors if needed to meet safety standards.

questions.question: While students load and unload a bus, the driver should:

options.text: Read a book.
Watch the process and keep an eye on the students.
Talk to other bus drivers.
Listen to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the process and keep an eye on the students.
questions.explanation: The driver must watch students as they enter and exit the bus. Make sure they don't get caught in doors or handrails. Also watch to make sure students move safely away from the bus after exiting.

questions.question: When conducting a vehicle inspection, you must show each of the following, except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off, or that the gauge shows increasing or normal oil pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge, if equipped, rises to the normal operating range.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that the oil pressure gauge works. It should show normal oil pressure or the warning light should turn off. If the vehicle has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature. The oil pressure gauge should not be related to brake use.

questions.question: When asked to make a lane change during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Make the necessary traffic checks first.
Not use your mirrors.
Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow the instructions.
Not make the lane change if you don't want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make the necessary traffic checks first.
questions.explanation: You will make several lane changes during the driving skills test. Check traffic first and use your signals. Change lanes smoothly when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: During the skills test, if making a turn that requires a stop, you should:

options.text: Skid to a stop.
Stop after the stop line to get a better view.
Allow your vehicle to roll.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly before the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels pointed straight and do not let the vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see its rear tires.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up is when you stop and pull forward to gain a better position. Simply stopping without pulling forward is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: When checking tire condition during the vehicle inspection, you should:

options.text: Ensure that the insides of the tires are more worn than the outsides of the tires.
Ensure that the outsides of the tires are more worn than the insides of the tires.
Ensure that the middles of the tires are more worn than the outsides of the tires.
Ensure that the tires have even wear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure that the tires have even wear.
questions.explanation: Check that tire treads are worn evenly across the whole tire.

questions.question: Drivers should try to stop ____ away from students at a bus stop.

options.text: About 100 feet
At least 50 feet
At least 10 feet
Less than 10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 10 feet
questions.explanation: Stop the bus at least 10 feet away from students at a bus stop. This makes students walk toward the bus so you can see them and watch their movements.

questions.question: When should a bus start moving after students have boarded?

options.text: As soon as students enter the door
When students are near their seats but still standing
When all students are seated and facing forward
As soon as students cross the standee line

questions.correctAnswerText: When all students are seated and facing forward
questions.explanation: Wait until all students are seated and looking forward before moving the bus.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it
Pull forward past the space, then back into it
Pull forward into the space without passing it first
Back into the space without passing it first

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it, keeping your vehicle completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a school bus, you should:

options.text: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail
Stop 100 feet before the nearest rail
Stop 10 feet before the nearest rail
Cross the tracks without stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail
questions.explanation: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the rail. This gives you a good view of the tracks. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: A properly adjusted outside convex mirror should show:

options.text: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground
Where the front of each front tire touches the ground
The top of the bus
The muffler

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground
questions.explanation: The outside convex mirrors should show where the front of each rear tire touches the ground, one traffic lane on each side, and the entire side of the bus.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Parallel park
Inspect your tires
Monitor your gauges
Pull forward into a parking space

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park
questions.explanation: The test may include straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Outside flat mirrors should show ____ behind the bus.

options.text: One bus length
50 feet
Four bus lengths
1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Four bus lengths
questions.explanation: The outside mirrors should be adjusted so you can see 200 feet (or four bus lengths) behind the bus.

questions.question: If your bus's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:

options.text: You will have no working brakes
The brakes will work more slowly than usual
You will still have normal braking power
You should not use the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have normal braking power
questions.explanation: Your bus will still have normal braking power if the ABS stops working. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: When approaching students at a bus stop, you should stop:

options.text: As close as possible to the students
Within an arm's reach of the students
At least 10 feet away from the students
About 80 feet away from the students

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 10 feet away from the students
questions.explanation: Stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This lets you watch their movements closely as they walk to the bus.

questions.question: A school bus stop:

options.text: Can be added by the driver if needed
Should be voted on by students
May change depending on weather
Should be set up by school district officials

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be set up by school district officials
questions.explanation: Do not change a bus stop location without written permission from school district officials.

questions.question: Outside mirrors on a school bus should be adjusted:

options.text: Before a trip starts
During a trip
After students board the bus
After a trip ends

questions.correctAnswerText: Before a trip starts
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before you begin a trip. Proper mirror adjustment keeps all students and other vehicles safe.
